acv.quote: Ninety-five K ACV, on a two-year term.

data.reason: Martin, the CFO, saw only a rate comparison and no figure for what failed orders cost Fernbrook. Sam blames price, but nothing on the page showed we weren't 'the same thing'.

trigger.action: Lead with big orders failing at checkout, not average acceptance gains.
trigger.why: Lucy came inbound because about one in twelve online orders failed, worst on the biggest baskets.
trigger.quote: about one in twelve online orders was failing at the payment step

decider.action: Tell the finance lead what failed orders cost, not just our rate.
decider.why: Sam never met Martin, who only saw a rate page and called us 'the same thing'.
decider.quote: Lucy told me. I never met him.

competitor.action: Say what stays broken when they only get a better rate.
competitor.why: Per Lucy via Sam, the bank cut its rate but offered no fix for failing orders.
competitor.quote: No new product, nothing. Just a better rate.

message.action: Keep explaining why big orders get declined and how we fix it.
message.why: Lucy nodded through Farah's explanation, while the average uplift slide never reached Martin.
message.quote: Lucy was nodding the whole way.

proof.action: Add a one-page cost of failed orders in the customer's own numbers.
proof.why: Lucy asked for a business case to hand Martin but got the deck and average uplift.
